Pros:

- Map simplicity makes it easier to read faster

- Health and Mana Bars are way better for your champion.

- Being able to rearrange the different champions is awesome when tabbing.

- Theres more breathing room, game feels open

Cons:

- Its hard to quickly scan for CS, Champion Ult CDs, Kills, etc.. above the map.

- Stats seem so small

- The items to the right of the spells feels overwhelming to glance at quickly.

- The ally champions display is so small and hard to gather info quickly. The pertinent information is really the champions health and mana, yet the picture of the champion is so large.

If There Were Fixes:

- Move the Items to the left of the portrait or allow the user to move them.

- Make the CS, Kills, etc.. Stand out more above the map or place it above the Champ Portrait..

- Allow the user to move ally character portraits, make the Health and Mana larger, and set the portrait smaller.

Extended but linked question: why doesn't poison oak or sumac grow in western (non coastal) states? I do understand the borders aren't as clearly defined as they are in the picture.

If this is better suited for /v/askscience let me know and I'll ask there.
Why doesn't poison ivy or sumac grow in California?

I'm no plant biologist, but from what I am aware of, there are two species of poison ivy and oak that grow in the western U.S.: western poison ivy and Pacific poison oak. At outdoors-y activities, camps, trails, etc., we in California are warned if these plants are present in the area and taught to recognize and avoid them, but that's the extent of my knowledge. I can't say for sure what is different between eastern and western species, the basis of their habitat requirements, etc. A quick google search told me that poison sumac grows in the eastern U.S. and requires swampy soil, so TIL we don't have poison sumac over here at all. We don't really have swamps or bogs, so that makes sense.
